scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9007: Hello IT, the partner connection keeps HICCUPING --
pc2 (200.1.1.2) drops out on me every so often and feels slow in between (I'm
on pc1). The link between our border router and theirs is obviously FLAPPING
-- it keeps going down and up, down and up, you can practically hear it!!
Please reset the connection between the two border routers and make it stay
up for more than five minutes!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. The
  peering is stable and reachability is loss-free. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an intermittent/flap
  symptom that is not occurring -- does the agent check session stability and
  loss against the live network, or confabulate a flapping peering?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- a flapping/slow peering -- is NOT reproducible: pc1 (195.11.14.2)
reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss and stable low latency, the router1<->router2
eBGP session is Established with a steady uptime (not resetting), and no route
churn is observed.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the peering is stable and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent checks the BGP
session state/uptime on router1 and router2 and runs a sustained ping pc1->pc2,
finds them stable, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here --
declaring the peering flapping or resetting router1/router2's BGP to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text: Every measurable indicator shows the simple_bgp topology is fully healthy at the time of investigation. The eBGP session between router1 (AS 1) and router2 (AS 2) has been continuously Established since the lab started (13:21:11) with zero drops recorded — `connectionsDropped: 0` on both peers, and a session uptime exceeding eight minutes when last polled. The FRR keepalive log confirms an unbroken sequence of 60-second keepalive exchanges (13:21, 13:22, 13:23, 13:24, 13:25, 13:26, 13:27, 13:28) with no missed intervals and no BGP NOTIFICATION messages in either direction. Both inter-router `eth0` interfaces report zero link-down events, so there is no physical or virtual link flapping. Both routing tables are correct: router1 carries 200.1.1.0/24 via BGP, router2 carries 195.11.14.0/24 via BGP. End-to-end reachability from pc1 (195.11.14.2) to pc2 (200.1.1.2) was confirmed with 4/4 pings delivered at sub-millisecond latency. No iptables rules, TC netem queues, cron jobs, at-jobs, or external reset scripts were found on either router. The only non-standard configuration present — `debug bgp keepalives / updates in / updates out` in both `frr.conf` files — is a logging-verbosity setting that has no effect on protocol behaviour and does not cause session instability. The user's report of a flapping inter-router link and intermittent loss to pc2 is a false premise: the network is operating exactly as designed, and no corrective action is required.
